subject: english
title: Imaginative, Discursive, Persuasive and Reflective Writing
explanation: Four modes, four contracts with the reader: imaginative writing builds worlds, discursive writing thinks aloud, persuasive writing pushes a position, reflective writing examines your own process. Strong writers switch modes on demand.
points: The four forms and what each promises the reader
Discursive writing: the essay that explores rather than argues
Persuasive and reflective modes: position and process
Drafting, editing and refining: the process behind all four
summary: The four writing modes each establish a different relationship with readers through distinct purposes—imaginative creates fictional worlds, discursive explores ideas analytically, persuasive argues a viewpoint, and reflective examines personal growth or understanding.
exam: Examiners penalise students who confuse modes by inserting persuasive arguments into reflective pieces or failing to maintain the imaginative contract by breaking into direct opinion statements.
